newsitem.title: USA: Climber dies on Alaska's Mount Hunter.
newsitem.headline: Climber dies on Alaska's Mount Hunter.

text.p: A falling block of ice and snow killed a mountain climber in Denali National Park, the National Park Service said on Monday.
Steve Mascioli, 38, of Bellingham, Washington, died in the accident that occurred on Friday on 14,573-foot (4,442-metres) Mount Hunter, a peak adjacent to Mount McKinley, the Park Service said.
The accident occurred at the 9,800-foot (3,000-metres) level of Hunter, the Park Service said.

Mascioli and his partner, Alan Kearney, also of Bellingham, were ascending the Moonflower route on Mount Hunter's North Buttress, one of the most difficult ice climbs in the Alaska Range, the Park Service said.

J.D. Swed, chief mountaineering ranger for Denali National Park, said it took Kearney a day and a half to reach the McKinley base camp at the 7,200-foot (2,200-metres) level of the Kahiltna Glacier, where he was able to notify authorities of the accident.
The climbers, both well-experienced, had no radio with them, Swed said.
